business_summary: International Seaways, Inc. (NYSE: INSW) is a US-listed international tanker owner operating a fleet of roughly 70 vessels, including four on order, across the principal crude and product tanker asset classes (VLCC, Suezmax, Aframax/LR2), giving it direct spot and time-charter exposure to Gulf-transit tonnage economics.

exposure_summary.narrative: INSW sits on the crude-tanker-tonnage link, the one CHOKE_POINT on this chain with deep listed coverage: roughly a third of effective fleet capacity is absorbed by the Cape of Good Hope detour, and cited quarterly TCE earnings more than doubled year over year across tanker classes during the crisis. FY2025 companyfacts shows revenue of $843.3M, a 40.96% operating margin and a net debt to EBITDA proxy of 0.88x, an unusually clean balance sheet for a capital-intensive shipowner.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: No Hormuz-specific or crude-tanker-segment revenue percentage is broken out in companyfacts this run; INSW's fleet spans crude and product tankers and companyfacts does not split Gulf-transit voyages from the rest.
